title: Prefill explicit L2::128B cache-hint attribution probe
decision: The single-round measurements show no consistent meaningful benefit. The retained native NVVM exporter was restored. These measurements do not replace the repeated final performance results.
conclusions: The saved reference PTX has no explicit L2::128B qualifier; the assembler produces its LTC128B SASS modifier from a condition not established by this investigation.
The hinted and plain inline-PTX kernels differ only by the LTC128B bit at 24 static LDGSTS instructions in each kernel. Independent raw ELF .text comparisons confirm all other code bytes match.

The retained native and plain inline-PTX static kernels are encoding-identical. Runtime kernels have different allocation and scheduling, so a direct native-to-hinted runtime comparison cannot isolate the hint.

Runtime hinted medians are 16.096 us in both modes; plain-control medians are 16.095 us in both modes. Their separate matched reference medians also vary. These single rounds do not establish a useful hint effect.

semantics.copy: The 16-byte cg copy keeps its original dynamic source-byte operand, including partial-atom and zero-byte copies. Source/destination calculations and caller-owned commit/wait/synchronization remain unchanged. The 4/8-byte native ca emission is unchanged.
semantics.inline_asm: The control and hinted forms use the same side-effecting inline PTX and memory clobber. Their source code differs only by .L2::128B.
semantics.target: L2::128B is a prefetch-size performance hint introduced in PTX 7.4, supported on sm_80 and newer. This probe uses the existing sm_120a target; it makes no general cache-policy or target-version change.

methodology.timing: Nsight Systems kernel-active duration from CUPTI kernel end minus start. One round of 31 measured launches follows 100 warmups; each report retains raw samples, trace metadata, execution order, exact commands and correctness results.
methodology.timing_limitation: One round per case is exploratory. Nsight Compute duration is not used. No significance or exact latency decomposition is claimed.
methodology.build_provenance: Frozen binary/CUBIN hashes and build manifests identify each candidate. A report source_snapshot describes files at measurement time and is explicitly not binary build provenance; use rust_build.manifest for the compiled candidate.
methodology.sass: Compared every instruction and control word, then independently compared raw ELF .text bytes. Disassembly ran sequentially in distinct directories after discarding outputs from a concurrent cuobjdump temporary-file collision.
methodology.gpu_work: The saved timing reports contain the parent-run GPU measurements. Preparing this durable analysis performed no GPU execution or build.

content.aggregation: median of each round's kernel samples, then median of round medians
content.runner_event_times: retained in runner_report; excluded from kernel-active summaries

source_snapshot.scope: current attention sources and selected compiler/API files; not binary build provenance

methodology.execution: sequential, each snapshot directory as working directory
methodology.why_sequential: Concurrent cuobjdump calls in the same working directory with identical input basenames collided in temporary files; those initial outputs were discarded and regenerated sequentially.
methodology.instruction_equivalence: Compared all PCs, operands, lower 64-bit encodings and upper 64-bit control/encoding words, then independently compared raw ELF .text sections.
methodology.instruction_count: Static instructions, including padding NOPs; these are not dynamic execution counts.
methodology.timing: No timing or GPU execution performed by this analysis.

semantics.source_size_operand: unchanged, including partial-atom and zero-byte copy

whole-kernel SASS may differ due to inline asm or assembler scheduling; compare plain control
content.preparation_status: Scratch preparation performed no builds; parent subsequently built both variants and analysis inspected frozen CUBINs.

sass_comparison.result: Plain vs hint: only LTC128B bit at 24 copies per kernel. Native vs plain: static kernels identical, runtime kernels rescheduled/reallocated.

content.native_vs_inline_ptx: Identical CUBIN hashes for arbitrary bytes, and for select(16, 0), respectively. The native NVVM operation is not the cause of ZFILL.
content.bytecount: Arbitrary byte counts produce ZFILL. The same native operation with select(16, 0) produces a predicate operand without ZFILL. Preserve arbitrary byte counts for partially valid atoms.
content.predicate_polarity: The ignore-source PTX predicate uses !P while selected bytecount uses P; polarity alone does not imply additional instructions.

thread_range.explanation: Emitter.index leaves the final coordinate quotient unbounded. Without a tid<128 proof this introduces a column carry and permits partial atoms. The reference directly bounds the column and selects source bytes from {0,16}. Addresses agree for the required participating thread IDs.

l2_hint.reference_source: MLIR copy atom cache=global; saved PTX has plain cp.async.cg.shared.global with no L2::128B hint.
l2_hint.reassembly: Reassembling the saved reference PTX with installed ptxas reproduces LTC128B in SASS. The assembler selects it from this context; the exact enabling condition is not established.
l2_hint.minimal_probes: Native and plain inline PTX probes omit LTC128B, even with reqntid128, aligned pointers, generic entry pointers or contiguous tid*16 addresses. Explicit L2::128B adds LTC128B independently of ZFILL.
l2_hint.recommendation: No explicit reference cache hint was found; do not add an arbitrary L2 hint to match one SASS modifier.

causal.interpretation: Separate single-round medians; no useful benefit demonstrated.
